answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil floods by charging a uniqueness bond that only unlocks after many epochs of peer-attested work. Picture the registry as a still lagoon: one honest vessel is welcome, yet a swarm of clones must sink a marble of collateral for every extra hull. Those deposits are cut from the same timber of spendable balance, and coordinated wallets that grade or vote in lockstep forfeit the bond, so fake identities cost more than they can steal.
